title: Whom he sees not (1 John 4:20)
hook: how can you love God whom you don't see if you don't love your brother
tomorrow: keep yourselves in the love of God

segments.voice: Yesterday, perfect charity casts out fear. Your line was love casts out fear.

In Dostoevsky's novel The Brothers Karamazov, the old monk Zosima tells about a doctor who once admitted something embarrassing. The more he loved humanity in general, the less he loved actual people in particular. In his dreams he'd gladly die for the human race. But put him in a room with one real person for a day, and he couldn't stand the way they blew their nose or how slowly they ate. Some mornings that doctor is in the mirror. John, near the end of his first letter, catches the same trick and turns it toward God.
screen: `DOSTOEVSKY'S DOCTOR.` → `HUMANITY, YES. PEOPLE, NO.` → `JOHN TURNS IT TOWARD GOD.`

segments.voice: John has just said that God is love and that love casts out fear. Then he brings it down to earth with a thud. The Douay-Rheims: "If any man say, I love God, and hateth his brother; he is a liar. For he that loveth not his brother, whom he seeth, how can he love God, whom he seeth not?" Liar is a strong word, and John means it. Not mistaken, not still growing: lying. Love for God can stay very safe. God doesn't interrupt you, borrow your car, or chew loudly. Earlier in this chapter John says no one has ever seen God. So where does love for the unseen God get tested? On the seen. The coworker. The brother-in-law. The roommate. If you can't manage the one in front of you, whose face you know, what makes you think you're managing the one you've never seen? And right after, he spells out the commandment: whoever loves God must love his brother also. The two loves aren't rivals. They're one love, facing two directions. Catholics act this out at Mass. Just before Communion, before receiving the Lord they cannot see, people may turn to whoever is next to them and offer a sign of peace: a handshake, a nod, sometimes to a stranger, sometimes to the family member they were arguing with in the car. Jesus said something like it: if you remember at the altar that your brother has something against you, go first and be reconciled, then come back and offer your gift.
screen: `IF ANY MAN SAY, I LOVE GOD...` · `NO ONE HAS EVER SEEN GOD.` · `ONE LOVE, FACING TWO WAYS.` · `THE SIGN OF PEACE BEFORE COMMUNION.` · then, large: `WHOM HE SEETH, AND WHOM HE SEETH NOT.`

segments.voice: Think of the person nearest your life right now, the one you'll see today: not the easiest, just the nearest. Picture their face, the things that wear on you too, and find one small way to love them: a kind word, patience with a habit, listening to the end of a story. If you pray, hold them before God by name; if not, look at them kindly in your mind.
Whom he sees not. First John four: love for the God no one has seen is tested on the brother and sister we can see. Today's word.
Your line: love the one you see. One love, facing two directions. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: At Mass, after the Lord's Prayer and before Communion, Catholics may exchange a sign of peace with the people around them, and the Church teaches that love of God and love of neighbor are inseparable.

fork.setup: you're on your way to Mass, and you just argued with your brother in the car. now he's in the pew beside you, and the sign of peace is coming. what does the reading point you toward?
options: skip it and focus on God.
offer him peace, because love for God shows up in love for him.
wait for him to apologize first.
fork.reveal: John asks how you can love God whom you don't see if you don't love the brother you do. Jesus says it too: be reconciled first, then bring your gift.

original.note: Greek: brother (1 John 4:20). in the letter it means fellow believers, men and women alike.

trapdoor: what you thought: it's easier to love people than to love God.
what it means: loving the unseen God can stay safe and abstract; John says it gets tested on the people right in front of you.
what a scholar hears: an argument from lesser to greater, after 'no man hath seen God at any time' (4:12); 4:21 joins the two loves as one commandment.
recall: God, maker of sun, moon and stars

chat.says: I love God, I just can't stand my brother-in-law. Is that really so bad?
options: John says love for the unseen God is tested on the people you see, even hard ones.
Not at all; loving God is what counts, and people are a separate matter.
Only if you tell him so; feelings you keep to yourself don't count.
chat.meaning: John: whoever doesn't love the brother he sees can't love the God he doesn't see. One love, facing two directions.
